content: No, that is not true. In Switzerland, the retirement age for women is not a fixed age of 64 for all birth cohorts. The retirement age is based on the year of birth and is determined by the Swiss Federal Act on Old-Age and Survivors' Pensions (AHVG). As of recent reforms, women born after 1957 generally retire at age 64, but those born earlier may retire at a younger age. The retirement age has been gradually increasing in recent years to reflect longer life expectancy and changes in the pension system.
